title: 2.3.30 Print Settings Advisor
description: Write a switch on filamentType with at least four cases and a default, printing a recommended temperature and speed for each. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Create a variable to switch on
steps.instructions: Create a variable called filamentType and assign it one of: 'PLA', 'ABS', 'PETG', 'TPU'.

steps.title: Write the switch
steps.instructions: Write a switch on filamentType with a case for 'PLA', 'ABS', 'PETG', and 'TPU'. Each case must print a recommended temperature and a recommended print speed for that filament, and what you print must include the words "temperature" and "speed": you choose reasonable numbers. Add a default that prints a message for a filament type you don't recognize. End every case with a break.

steps.title: Comment where fall-through would happen
steps.instructions: Above one of your case labels, write a comment explaining exactly what would print for that filament (and which cases below it) if its break were removed. Use the word "break" in your comment. Don't actually remove the break: the comment is the deliverable.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "2.3.30 Print Settings Advisor". The task they were given: Create a variable called filamentType and assign it one of: 'PLA', 'ABS', 'PETG', 'TPU'. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
